knowledge_point.title: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-8y &=8 \\ 3x-7y &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -8 & 8 \\ 3 & -7 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -8 & 8 \\ 3 & -7 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -4 & 4 \\ 3 & -7 & 2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & -10\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-4y &=-2 \\ 4x-7y &=-3.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & -2 \\ 4 & -7 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & -2 \\ 4 & -7 & -3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 4 & -7 & -3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=-1 \\ y &=1,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=1$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(1)=-1\,⇒\,x=1.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=1$ and $y=1.$

\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -8 & 12 \\ 3 & -7 & 3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -4 & 6 \\ 3 & -7 & 3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -4 & 6 \\ 0 & 5 & -15\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -4 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}

knowledge_point.title: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=-7 \\ 2x+4y &=6.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -7 \\ 2 & 4 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -7 \\ 2 & 4 & 6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -7 \\ 0 & 10 & 20\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{10}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=-7 \\ y &=2,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=2$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-3(2)=-7\,⇒\,x=-1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-1$ and $y=2.$
